Motion · A small, repeatable project

Make a three-second hero loop with Remotion.

Use official Agent Skills in Codex or Claude Code to create a short website graphic. Start from a real composition you can inspect, render and adapt.

Explore Remotion Agent Skills →

Download the sample MP4 · Download static poster

1. Choose your starting point

Remotion

The React-based project and renderer produce the actual video. You need Node.js/npm and a browser runtime; the first render can download one.

Official getting started guide

Codex or Claude Code

Your existing coding agent reads the Remotion skills and edits the composition. Skills supply instructions; they do not install an agent or replace the renderer.

Official skills and supported agents

New to Remotion? In a parent folder outside an existing Git repository, create a blank project. Follow its installation prompts, then open the new folder in your coding agent.

npx create-video@latest --yes --blank hero-loop
cd hero-loop

Already have a Remotion project? Skip scaffolding. In its project folder, add the official skills:

npx remotion skills add

Follow the installer’s prompts to select Codex or Claude Code and the project scope. Review the selected destination before confirming. If Remotion is not yet installed, the documented alternative is:

npx skills add remotion-dev/skills

Choose one installation route. These commands fetch current upstream files. In PowerShell, use npx.cmd if script execution policy blocks npx. Select a relevant skill from your host’s menu, or explicitly ask it to use the installed Remotion skills. Exact invocation depends on the host.

2. Give the agent a bounded brief

Paste this in your project’s agent session. It asks for a decorative website asset with a readable still state.

Use the installed official Remotion skills for this project.
Make one original 3-second hero loop: 1280 x 720, 30 fps, 90 frames.
Use only React, CSS and simple shapes; no external images, fonts or audio.
Keep the headline still and readable: "Make room for a clearer idea."
Animate 3 small cards labelled Plan, Draft and Refine with subtle periodic motion.
Derive all motion from useCurrentFrame(); no CSS animation or wall-clock time.
Make the period exactly 90 frames, so the loop wraps without a visible jump.
Register a composition named HeroLoop and produce an H.264 MP4 plus frame-0 poster.
Keep text inside safe margins. Supply a static poster and user-controlled playback
for the website. Do not autoplay, publish, install unrelated tools or use paid APIs.
List the render command and verify width, height, frame rate, count and duration.
If rendering is unavailable, say so; do not claim that a valid source file is a rendered video.

Begin with the umbrella skill remotion-best-practices when unsure which specific skill to use. Review the generated composition before running it.

3. Run the supplied example

Want a known starting point? The source download contains our original composition and a small package manifest. Extract it to a new folder, open a terminal there, then install dependencies and render. It is separate from the agent-skill installation above.

Download example source

npm install
npm run render
npm run poster
Use the composition in an existing project

Copy the downloaded index.tsx to src/hero-loop.tsx without replacing your existing entry file. It registers its own root. Render it directly:

npx remotion render src/hero-loop.tsx HeroLoop out/hero-loop.mp4 --codec=h264

The example keeps its headline static while three cards move with a sine/cosine phase derived from the frame number. Its phase repeats every 90 frames; the hypothetical frame 90 matches frame 0. Frame 89 should flow into frame 0, not duplicate it.

4. Verify the export and the loop

Rendered example: the supplied composition was rendered with Remotion 4.0.545 on 2026-11-22. Metadata check: 1280 × 720, 30 fps, 90 frames, 3.000 seconds, H.264, no audio. The MP4 is 431581 bytes. This verifies the example render, not native agent installation or a measured skill improvement.

  1. Probe the output: if FFprobe is installed, run the command below. Expect 1280 × 720, 30/1 frame rate, 90 frames and 3.000000 seconds.
  2. Watch several cycles: inspect the wrap from the last frame to the first. Check that the static headline stays readable and no shape jumps or clips.
  3. Check the website: use a poster and visible playback controls. Retain a static alternative for people who prefer reduced motion; this sample never starts automatically.
  4. Check delivery size: choose an encoding and resolution appropriate to your page. A short clip can still hurt load time; do not preload a decorative video unnecessarily.
ffprobe -v error -count_frames -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=width,height,r_frame_rate,nb_read_frames:format=duration -of json hero-loop.mp4

If rendering fails: read the actual error first. Common blockers include missing project dependencies and the initial browser download. A successful source edit is not a successful render. Keep Remotion package versions aligned.

Before commercial use: check Remotion’s current license eligibility and terms for your organisation and version. Agent access, rendering infrastructure and any external media can have separate costs. This source uses only original text and simple shapes.
